# Branchable CPU scheduling experiments, protocol 3.0

The goal is an exact event log and final state certificate for a staged,
interleaved packet scheduler. Extend the provided computational library. Its
baseline packet objects, rank policies, FIFO/PIFO scheduling and ordered-storage
interface do not implement this complete contract. Equivalent data structures
and module organizations are accepted.

Entry `submission/cli.py` reads one UTF-8 JSON request through EOF, emits one
UTF-8 JSON response and exits zero. Whitespace and object order do not matter;
array order does. Output has exactly the specified keys and types. Integer
fields require JSON integer tokens, never booleans or floats. Invalid UTF-8,
malformed JSON, duplicate keys at any depth, nonfinite values (including `1e999`)
or trailing JSON values return exactly `{"error":"invalid"}` with exit zero.
Other inputs satisfy the schema; other schema-error handling is unspecified.
No diagnostics on stdout.

## Request and initial state

Root: `{"runs":[RUN,...]}`; zero runs is legal. Each run has exactly:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `banks` | M physical PIFOs, 1..16 |
| `load_balancers` | L dispatch instances, 1..8 |
| `fifo_bytes` | Capacity of each bank's staging FIFO, 1..2147483647 |
| `pifo_bytes` | Capacity of each bank's PIFO, 1..2147483647 |
| `refill_batch` | Packet transfer limit per refill, 1..32 |
| `sample_period` | P admitted packets per automatic sample, 1..100000 |
| `borders` | Strictly increasing integer [0,b1,...,U], 1..64 ranges, 1<=U<=2147483647 |
| `policy` | One of the policy objects below |
| `events` | Ordered command arrays below, possibly empty |

Range r is [b[r],b[r+1]). Every partition in a run has endpoints 0,U. Classify
using min(rank,U-1); the actual rank remains unclipped for priority and metrics.
Initially queues are empty, logical service tick t=0, next service bank p=0,
next load balancer l=0, admitted-since-sample a=0, and history H[r]=0. Dispatch
counters C have shape [L][M][R], with C[l][q][r]=1 when q < (r modulo M), else 0.
This initial stagger is a counter bias, not a resident population.

All arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic. An enqueue's immutable tie ordinal
is its zero-based index in the complete event array. Output indices and these
ordinals never rewind on restore.

## Rank policies

| Policy object | Rank assigned on every enqueue attempt |
|---|---|
| `{"kind":"fifo"}` | Increment a policy counter, initially zero, and use its new value |
| `{"kind":"sp","levels":[[flow,level],...]}` | Configured level, 0..2147483647 |
| `{"kind":"sff"}` | Supplied packet flow_size, 0..2147483647 |
| `{"kind":"wfq","weights":[[flow,weight],...]}` | Set F[flow]=max(F[flow],V)+ceil(length*1048576/weight[flow]); use the new F[flow] |

WFQ starts at V=0, F=0 for each declared flow. Successful service updates
V=max(V,served rank). Drops, cancellation and idle visits do not update V.
Weights are integers 1..1024; these are quantized finish tags, not floating-point
WFQ. Level/weight tables have unique flow IDs and at most 10000 entries. Every
used SP/WFQ flow is declared. A weight update affects future attempts only;
existing ranks and finish tags remain. Rejected attempts still advance FIFO/WFQ
rank state. FIFO/SFF need no flow table.

## Admission, service and lag

Each bank has an arrival-ordered staging FIFO and a PIFO ordered by immutable
(rank,ordinal). Equal ranks are stable locally; cross-bank reordering is allowed.
The global live set includes both stages.

An enqueue uses current load balancer l and range r. Its bank q minimizes
C[l][q][r], ties by smallest bank index. The next l always advances modulo L,
even on rejection. Admission succeeds exactly when selected FIFO bytes plus
packet length <= fifo_bytes. There is no fallback bank or FIFO eviction. An
admitted packet starts with lag zero, increments its C entry and a. A rejected
packet is never live and does not change a or C.

A service opportunity visits exactly p, advances p modulo M, and increments t,
including idle visits; it never searches another bank. If that PIFO was already
nonempty, its head is served and frees bytes before a refill. If it was empty,
a refill supplies candidates before a head can be served; there is no additional
refill after this resulting pop. Policy post-service feedback belongs to the
successful pop, before a subsequent refill.

A refill transfers the first min(refill_batch,FIFO population) packets into its
PIFO. Of the resulting candidate set sorted by (rank,ordinal), retain the
longest prefix whose total bytes <= pifo_bytes. Evict the suffix in descending
(rank,ordinal) order. Newly transferred packets may be evicted; the retained
prefix may be empty. All transfers free FIFO bytes; evictions immediately leave
the global live set. FIFO rejection and PIFO pushout are distinct losses.

After any associated refill/pushout, a successful service's rank_error is the
number of other live packets with strictly smaller rank. Report the served
packet's previously accumulated lag. It leaves the live set; every remaining
strictly lower-rank resident gains one lag. Equal ranks do not contribute. Lag
counts priority overtakes while live, not elapsed ticks. Stage changes preserve
lag. Idle visits change neither lag nor policy virtual time. EOF does not drain.

## Sampling and partition migration

A sample captures X[r]=sum(C[l][q][r]) before normalization. Each fixed (l,r)
counter row is translated by subtracting its minimum over q. Replace history by
H[r]=floor(H[r]/2)+X[r] and reset a=0. X includes initial bias and retained
counter differences. Immediately after an admission makes a=P, an automatic
sample appends a log row after that enqueue. An explicit sample is identical.

Repartition changes active borders and conservatively re-expresses every
C[l][q] vector and H on the new ranges. Old interval [b,c) with integer mass m
contributes exactly this amount to new interval [u,v):

`floor(m*clamp(v-b,0,c-b)/(c-b)) - floor(m*clamp(u-b,0,c-b)/(c-b))`.

Sum contributions from all old ranges. This prefix-quantized projection
preserves each vector's total. Do not round overlaps independently, reset or
normalize counters, or relocate residents. Pointers, a, policy state and lags
are retained. The external command supplies borders; choosing them is out of scope.

## Commands and log certificate

Each command appends the row below, where i is its event-array index. Only
automatic samples append an extra row. A dequeue command appends n rows.
IDs, flow IDs and checkpoint names are integers 0..2147483647. Enqueue IDs are
unique across the entire command array, including discarded branches. Lengths
are 1..1000000 and every supplied flow_size is 0..2147483647. Inspect/cancel may name an unknown or terminal ID.

| Command | Appended row |
|---|---|
| `["enqueue",id,flow,length,flow_size]` | `[i,"enqueue",id,rank,l,r,q,accepted]`; accepted is boolean; then any automatic sample row |
| `["dequeue",n]`, n>=1 | `[i,"dequeue",old_t,q,id,rank,rank_error,lag,evicted_ids]` per visit; idle id/rank=null and error/lag=0 |
| `["sample"]` | `[i,"sample",X,new_H]` |
| `["repartition",new_borders]` | `[i,"repartition",new_R]` |
| `["cancel",id]` | `[i,"cancel",id,old_stage,old_bank,lag]`; absent ID has three nulls |
| `["inspect",id]` | `[i,"inspect",id,record]`; record=[rank,bank,stage,length,flow,lag], or null |
| `["weight",flow,new_weight]` | `[i,"weight",flow,new_weight]`; WFQ only, declared flow |
| `["save",name]` | `[i,"save",name]` |
| `["restore",name]` | `[i,"restore",name]` |

Stage strings are `fifo` and `pifo`. Cancellation immediately frees that stage's
bytes and removes the live packet without service, rank recalculation, counter
decrement or sampling. Historical admission counters do not decrease on any
departure, pushout or cancellation.

Save records the entire scheduler and rank-policy state and replaces an older
save of that name. Restore recovers it independently of all subsequent mutations;
repeated restores are allowed. The name registry is outside saved state and
never rewinds. Every restore names a saved slot. Save/restore cause no sampling
or service. Old branch output stays in the log, so IDs may appear in multiple
branch histories. No particular checkpoint representation or serialization is
required.

## Response and final state

Root: `{"runs":[{"log":[...],"state":STATE},...]}` in input order. STATE has
exactly these keys certifying the final active branch:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `tick` | Service opportunities on the active branch, t |
| `load_balancer` | Next dispatch instance l |
| `service_bank` | Next service bank p |
| `sample_progress` | Admitted-since-sample a |
| `borders` | Current complete [0,...,U] array |
| `counters` | C in [L][M][R] order |
| `history` | H in range order |
| `policy` | Policy certificate below |
| `queues` | M objects, each `{"fifo":[ids in FIFO order],"pifo":[ids in priority order],"fifo_bytes":integer,"pifo_bytes":integer}` |
| `lags` | [id,lag] pairs for every live ID, sorted by ID |

Policy certificates are exactly: FIFO `{"kind":"fifo","time":counter}`; SP
`{"kind":"sp","levels":[[flow,level],...]}`; SFF `{"kind":"sff"}`; or WFQ
`{"kind":"wfq","virtual_time":V,"weights":[[flow,weight],...],"finish":[[flow,F],...]}`.
Flow tables sort by flow ID and include every declared flow, even unused ones.
Results can exceed 2^53 and must remain exact integers.

This CPU control/data-state model omits transmission time, end-to-end transport,
pipeline-cycle latency, strict flow ordering and universal rank-error bounds.
No hardware rate or optimization-quality score is requested.

## Complete whole-request bounds

At most 8 runs, 100000 expanded operations total, and 60000 enqueues. Ordinary
events contribute one operation; dequeue contributes n instead. Each run has at
most 64 distinct save names. Input <=16 MiB. Supporting ordinary files are allowed
in submission; there is no exact-file-list trap.
All supporting files and directories, even unused files and empty directories,
obey the portable relative pathname limits in `RESOURCES.md`: UTF-8, <=1024
bytes including separators from the submission root, <=255 bytes per component.
Every entry also has <=64 relative path components, including its final filename
or directory name; all supporting and empty directories count. A file therefore
has at most 63 parent directories. Violations are candidate-format errors before
execution; see `RESOURCES.md`.

The following control-plane work bounds use input only. Per run let E be enqueue
count and Rmax the largest range count. Potential automatic samples A is
floor(E/sample_period), except use **E** whenever any restore command occurs:
restores can recover older nonzero sample progress. This conservative upper
bound does not depend on actual admissions. Let S be explicit sample count and
K be save+restore count. The batch sums of `L*M*Rmax*(A+S+K)` and, separately,
`L*M*Rold*Rnew` over repartitions are each <=4000000. The sum of
`Rmax*(A+S)` is <=200000. For Rold use Rmax if any restore occurs; otherwise use
the latest input partition size. These published bounds prevent unbounded
control-array/output work; no additional hidden work constraint applies.
====
# Execution and public development profiles

Submit a directory containing `cli.py` and every required module/data file.
Extra ordinary supporting files are allowed. The complete submission is <=8 MiB
and <=256 filesystem entries, including directories. Files must be regular,
nonsymlink and link count one; no special files. The entry is UTF-8 Python.
No particular internal algorithm, class layout or exact file list is required.

Every file and directory name must form a UTF-8 relative POSIX pathname of at
most 1024 bytes from the submission root, including `/` separators, with each
component at most 255 UTF-8 bytes. The root's absolute staging prefix is excluded.
These bounds apply to all supporting entries, including unused files and empty
directories. For example, `pkg/data.bin` uses 12 bytes; count bytes, not Unicode
characters. Pathnames cannot contain empty, `.` or `..` components. A violation
is a candidate submission-format error, rejected before candidate execution.
The public validator is `submission_paths.py`.
Every relative pathname also has at most 64 slash-separated components, counting
the final file or directory name and excluding the submission root. Thus
`pkg/data.bin` has two components; a file may have at most 63 parent directories,
and an empty supporting directory may be 64 levels below the root. This applies
to all entries, used or unused. Deeper trees are candidate-format errors rejected
before execution; collection stops before copying the first over-limit entry.
This portable source-nesting limit keeps collection and temporary-tree cleanup
within the documented parent FD budget; it does not change scored FD limits.

The scored command is `python3 -I -B /workspace/submission/cli.py`, cwd

file, and zero core bytes. Fork/vfork/clone and threads are denied; RLIMIT_NPROC 64
is a secondary limit. No CPU affinity change or exclusive core is used.
Input <=16 MiB, stdout <=32 MiB and stderr <=1 MiB. The full published batch is one

Execution is nonroot in an allowlisted local chroot with frozen runtime/source.
Only `/workspace/tmp` is a writable storage directory, cleared before each outer isolated invocation. Public sanity children share that
outer invocation's scratch; do not depend on leftover files.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Public-only sanity cases, executed through bounded subprocess pipes."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
from runner import run, same, strict_json
from submission_paths import validate_relative_path


def collect(source, target):
    if source.is_symlink() or not source.is_dir():
        raise ValueError('submission directory required')
    total = entries = 0
    target.mkdir()
    for base, dirs, files in os.walk(source, followlinks=False):
        rel = Path(base).relative_to(source)
        for name in dirs + files:
            validate_relative_path((rel/name).as_posix())
            path = Path(base)/name
            info = path.lstat()
            entries += 1
            if entries > 256:
                raise ValueError('submission entry cap')
            dest = target/rel/name
            if stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                dest.mkdir()
            elif stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_nlink == 1:
                total += info.st_size
                if total > 8*1024**2:
                    raise ValueError('submission byte cap')
                data = path.read_bytes()
                if len(data) != info.st_size:
                    raise ValueError('submission changed during collection')
                dest.write_bytes(data)
                dest.chmod(0o444)
            else:
                raise ValueError('unsafe submission entry')
    entry = target/'cli.py'
    entry.read_bytes().decode('utf-8')
    return entry


def main():
    if os.geteuid() == 0:
        raise RuntimeError('run as a nonprivileged user')
    source = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) == 2 else 'submission')
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    cases = [((here/'examples/request.json').read_bytes(),
              strict_json((here/'examples/response.json').read_bytes())),
             (b'{"runs":[]}', {'runs':[]})]
    for data in (b'', b'not json', b'{} {}', b'{"runs":[],"runs":[]}',
                 b'{"x":NaN}', b'{"x":1e999}', b'\xff'):
        cases.append((data, {'error':'invalid'}))
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='public-check-', dir='/workspace/tmp') as temp:
        entry = collect(source, Path(temp)/'submission')
        for index, (data, expected) in enumerate(cases):
            actual = strict_json(run(entry, data))
            if not same(actual, expected):
                raise RuntimeError(f'public case {index} mismatch')
    print(f'public sanity: {len(cases)} child invocations passed')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        main()
    except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt) as exc:
        print(f'public sanity failed: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

"""Published submission pathname limits, shared by public collection/staging."""

MAX_RELATIVE_PATH_BYTES = 1024
MAX_COMPONENT_BYTES = 255
MAX_PATH_COMPONENTS = 64


class SubmissionPathError(ValueError):
    pass


def validate_relative_path(relative_path, *, max_bytes=MAX_RELATIVE_PATH_BYTES,
                           max_components=MAX_PATH_COMPONENTS):
    """Count UTF-8 bytes, including '/' separators, without a staging prefix."""
    name = str(relative_path)
    components = name.split('/')
    if not name or any(part in ('', '.', '..') for part in components):
        raise SubmissionPathError('candidate format error: non-relative submission pathname')
    if len(components) > max_components:
        raise SubmissionPathError(f'candidate format error: submission relative pathname exceeds {max_components} components')
    try:
        encoded = name.encode('utf-8')
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        raise SubmissionPathError('candidate format error: submission pathname must be UTF-8') from None
    if len(encoded) > max_bytes:
        raise SubmissionPathError(f'candidate format error: submission relative pathname exceeds {max_bytes} UTF-8 bytes')
    if any(len(part.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_COMPONENT_BYTES for part in components):
        raise SubmissionPathError('candidate format error: submission pathname component exceeds 255 UTF-8 bytes')

    total, entries, stack = 0, 0, [path]

        try:

"""Ordered-storage module: versioned copy-on-write treaps (protocol 3.0).

Two node layouts are used, both plain lists so that copying a node is a single
slice and an isolated checkpoint of a whole structure is one root reference:

  lean  [key, rec, prio, left, right, stamp]                   bank PIFOs
  fat   [key, rec, prio, left, right, size, val, lazy, stamp]  global live set

``key``   ordering key; ``(rank, ordinal)`` tuples for both layouts.
``rec``   the packet record that occupies the node.
``prio``  treap priority (deterministic, structural only).
``size``  subtree population (fat layout), used for rank-order statistics.
``val``   the node's own accumulated lag (fat layout).
``lazy``  a pending lag addition for every node of the subtree (fat layout).
``stamp`` version the node was produced in.  A node is copied before its first
          mutation in a later version, so saved checkpoints stay immutable while
          taking or reloading a checkpoint costs O(1).

Lag is stored as ``val + lazy`` per node, therefore "every remaining strictly
lower-rank resident gains one lag" is a single O(depth) subtree operation and
never walks the backlog.
"""

M64 = (1 << 64) - 1


class Priors:
    """Deterministic treap priority source; structure only, never observable."""

    __slots__ = ('state',)

    def __init__(self, seed=0x243F6A8885A308D3):
        self.state = seed & M64

    def take(self):
        s = self.state = (self.state + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) & M64
        z = s ^ (s >> 30)
        z = (z * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & M64
        z ^= z >> 27
        z = (z * 0x94D049BB133111EB) & M64
        return z ^ (z >> 31)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- lean layout


def lean_insert(node, key, rec, prio, ver):
    if node is None:
        return [key, rec, prio, None, None, ver]
    node = node[:] if node[5] != ver else node
    if key < node[0]:
        node[3] = lean_insert(node[3], key, rec, prio, ver)
        child = node[3]
        if child[2] > node[2]:
            node[3] = child[4]
            child[4] = node
            return child
    else:
        node[4] = lean_insert(node[4], key, rec, prio, ver)
        child = node[4]
        if child[2] > node[2]:
            node[4] = child[3]
            child[3] = node
            return child
    return node


def lean_merge(a, b, ver):
    if a is None:
        return b
    if b is None:
        return a
    if a[2] > b[2]:
        a = a[:] if a[5] != ver else a
        a[4] = lean_merge(a[4], b, ver)
        return a
    b = b[:] if b[5] != ver else b
    b[3] = lean_merge(a, b[3], ver)
    return b


def lean_delete(node, key, ver):
    if node is None:
        return None
    node = node[:] if node[5] != ver else node
    if key < node[0]:
        node[3] = lean_delete(node[3], key, ver)
    elif key > node[0]:
        node[4] = lean_delete(node[4], key, ver)
    else:
        return lean_merge(node[3], node[4], ver)
    return node


def lean_extract_min(node, ver):
    """Return (new root, node) for the smallest key; ``node`` must be live."""
    node = node[:] if node[5] != ver else node
    left = node[3]
    if left is None:
        return node[4], node
    node[3], out = lean_extract_min(left, ver)
    return node, out


def lean_extract_max(node, ver):
    """Return (new root, node) for the largest key; ``node`` must be live."""
    node = node[:] if node[5] != ver else node
    right = node[4]
    if right is None:
        return node[3], node
    node[4], out = lean_extract_max(right, ver)
    return node, out


def lean_find(node, key):
    while node is not None:
        k = node[0]
        if k == key:
            return node
        node = node[3] if key < k else node[4]
    return None


def lean_recs(node, out):
    """Append records in key order (loop on the right spine)."""
    while node is not None:
        lean_recs(node[3], out)
        out.append(node[1])
        node = node[4]

def _fat_push(node, ver):
    """Move ``node.lazy`` into its own value and both children (copy-on-write)."""
    lz = node[7]
    node[6] += lz
    node[7] = 0
    left = node[3]
    if left is not None:
        left = left[:] if left[8] != ver else left
        left[7] += lz
        node[3] = left
    right = node[4]
    if right is not None:
        right = right[:] if right[8] != ver else right
        right[7] += lz
        node[4] = right


def fat_insert(node, key, rec, prio, ver):
    if node is None:
        return [key, rec, prio, None, None, 1, 0, 0, ver]
    node = node[:] if node[8] != ver else node
    if node[7]:
        _fat_push(node, ver)
    if key < node[0]:
        node[3] = fat_insert(node[3], key, rec, prio, ver)
        node[5] += 1
        child = node[3]
        if child[2] > node[2]:
            node[3] = child[4]
            node[5] = 1 + (node[3][5] if node[3] is not None else 0) \
                        + (node[4][5] if node[4] is not None else 0)
            child[4] = node
            child[5] = 1 + node[5] + (child[3][5] if child[3] is not None else 0)
            return child
    else:
        node[4] = fat_insert(node[4], key, rec, prio, ver)
        node[5] += 1
        child = node[4]
        if child[2] > node[2]:
            node[4] = child[3]
            node[5] = 1 + (node[3][5] if node[3] is not None else 0) \
                        + (node[4][5] if node[4] is not None else 0)
            child[3] = node
            child[5] = 1 + node[5] + (child[4][5] if child[4] is not None else 0)
            return child
    return node


def fat_merge(a, b, ver):
    if a is None:
        return b
    if b is None:
        return a
    if a[2] > b[2]:
        a = a[:] if a[8] != ver else a
        if a[7]:
            _fat_push(a, ver)
        a[4] = fat_merge(a[4], b, ver)
        a[5] = 1 + (a[3][5] if a[3] is not None else 0) \
                  + (a[4][5] if a[4] is not None else 0)
        return a
    b = b[:] if b[8] != ver else b
    if b[7]:
        _fat_push(b, ver)
    b[3] = fat_merge(a, b[3], ver)
    b[5] = 1 + (b[3][5] if b[3] is not None else 0) \
              + (b[4][5] if b[4] is not None else 0)
    return b


def fat_pop(node, key, thr, ver, acc):
    """Remove ``key`` from the live set.

    ``thr`` is the served rank: when given, every remaining entry of strictly
    smaller rank gains one lag and is counted, which yields rank_error in the
    same descent.  Returns ``(new root, lag of the removed entry, count)``.
    """
    node = node[:] if node[8] != ver else node
    acc += node[7]
    k = node[0]
    if k == key:
        lag = acc + node[6]
        if node[7]:
            _fat_push(node, ver)
        return fat_merge(node[3], node[4], ver), lag, 0
    if k < key:
        add = thr is not None and k[0] < thr
        if add:
            node[6] += 1
            left = node[3]
            if left is not None:
                left = left[:] if left[8] != ver else left
                left[7] += 1
                node[3] = left
        node[4], lag, cnt = fat_pop(node[4], key, thr, ver, acc)
        if add:
            cnt += 1 + (node[3][5] if node[3] is not None else 0)
        node[5] -= 1
        return node, lag, cnt
    node[3], lag, cnt = fat_pop(node[3], key, thr, ver, acc)
    node[5] -= 1
    return node, lag, cnt


def fat_lag(root, key):
    """Lag of ``key`` or None when the entry is absent (read-only descent)."""
    acc = 0
    node = root
    while node is not None:
        acc += node[7]
        k = node[0]
        if k == key:
            return acc + node[6]
        node = node[3] if key < k else node[4]
    return None


def fat_pairs(node, acc, out):
    """Append ``(rec, lag)`` pairs in key order (loop on the right spine)."""
    while node is not None:
        a = acc + node[7]
        fat_pairs(node[3], a, out)
        out.append((node[1], a + node[6]))
        node = node[4]
        acc = a

"""Staged bank scheduler (protocol 3.0).

Each physical bank owns an arrival-ordered staging FIFO and a PIFO ordered by
the immutable ``(rank, ordinal)`` of its residents.  The global live set spans
both stages of every bank and is held in one rank-ordered order-statistic tree
that also carries the live lag accounting, so priority overtakes are charged
with a single O(depth) subtree operation instead of a backlog walk.

Service opportunities are fixed and cyclic: a visit touches bank ``p`` only,
advances ``p`` and the logical tick even when nothing is served.  Historical
admission counters never decrease; sampling and repartitioning re-express them
conservatively.  Checkpoints isolate whole branches; the name registry lives
outside the saved state and never rewinds.
"""

from bisect import bisect_right

from packet import Pkt
from algorithms import (SchedulingAlgorithm, FifoAlgorithm, SpAlgorithm,
                        pFabricAlgorithm, WFQAlgorithm, make_policy)
import treap

from treap import (Priors, lean_insert, lean_delete, lean_extract_min,
                   lean_extract_max, lean_find, lean_recs,
                   fat_insert, fat_pop, fat_lag, fat_pairs)


class Scheduler:
    """Baseline scheduling interface retained for library users."""

    def enqueue(self, pkt: Pkt) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")

    def dequeue(self):
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")


def _migrate_vector(vector, old_borders, new_borders, new_ranges):
    """Prefix-quantized projection of one counter vector onto new ranges."""
    out = [0] * new_ranges
    ranges = len(vector)
    for j in range(ranges):
        mass = vector[j]
        if not mass:
            continue
        low = old_borders[j]
        width = old_borders[j + 1] - low
        previous = 0
        for s in range(1, new_ranges + 1):
            x = new_borders[s] - low
            if x < 0:
                x = 0
            elif x > width:
                x = width
            value = (mass * x) // width
            out[s - 1] += value - previous
            previous = value
    return out


class StagedBankScheduler(Scheduler):
    """One run of the experiment: banks, policies, events, certificates."""

    def __init__(self, spec):
        self.M = int(spec['banks'])
        self.L = int(spec['load_balancers'])
        self.fifo_cap = int(spec['fifo_bytes'])
        self.pifo_cap = int(spec['pifo_bytes'])
        self.refill_batch = int(spec['refill_batch'])
        self.period = int(spec['sample_period'])
        self.borders = [int(x) for x in spec['borders']]
        self.R = len(self.borders) - 1
        self.ver = 0
        self.policy = make_policy(spec['policy'], 0)
        self.priors = Priors()

        self.t = 0
        self.p = 0
        self.l = 0
        self.a = 0

        M = self.M
        L = self.L
        R = self.R
        # Admission counters C[l][q][r], flattened, with the initial stagger
        # C[l][q][r] = 1 when q < (r modulo M).  The stagger is a counter bias,
        # not a resident population.
        self.C = [0] * (L * M * R)
        for l in range(L):
            base = l * M * R
            for r in range(R):
                limit = r % M
                for q in range(M):
                    if q < limit:
                        self.C[base + q * R + r] = 1
        self.H = [0] * R

        self.live = None
        self.pifo = [None] * M
        self.fifo = [[] for _ in range(M)]
        self.fhead = [0] * M
        self.fcnt = [0] * M
        self.fbytes = [0] * M
        self.pbytes = [0] * M
        self.fstamp = [0] * M
        self.registry = {}
        self.snaps = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ primitives

    def classify(self, rank):
        borders = self.borders
        if rank >= borders[-1]:
            rank = borders[-1] - 1
        elif rank < 0:
            rank = 0
        return bisect_right(borders, rank) - 1

    def _touch_fifo(self, q):
        if self.fstamp[q] != self.ver:
            self.fifo[q] = self.fifo[q][:]
            self.fstamp[q] = self.ver

    def _refill(self, q):
        """Move the head of the staging FIFO into the PIFO and apply pushout.

        Returns the identifiers evicted by pushout, in descending
        (rank, ordinal) order.
        """
        batch = self.refill_batch
        count = self.fcnt[q]
        if count < batch:
            batch = count
        ver = self.ver
        evicted = []
        if batch:
            fifo = self.fifo[q]
            head = self.fhead[q]
            pifo = self.pifo[q]
            bytes_used = self.pbytes[q]
            priors = self.priors.take
            cap = self.pifo_cap
            moved = 0
            while moved < batch:
                pkt = fifo[head]
                head += 1
                if pkt is None:        # cancelled while staged
                    continue
                moved += 1
                self.fbytes[q] -= pkt.length
                self.fcnt[q] -= 1
                pifo = lean_insert(pifo, (pkt.rank, pkt.oid), pkt,
                                   priors(), ver)
                bytes_used += pkt.length
                if bytes_used > cap:
                    pifo, node = lean_extract_max(pifo, ver)
                    over = node[1]
                    bytes_used -= over.length
                    self.live = fat_pop(self.live, (over.rank, over.oid),
                                        None, ver, 0)[0]
                    evicted.append(over.pktid)
            self.fhead[q] = head
            self.pifo[q] = pifo
            self.pbytes[q] = bytes_used
        elif self.pbytes[q] > self.pifo_cap:
            # Nothing transferred, but an over-capacity PIFO still pushes out.
            pifo = self.pifo[q]
            bytes_used = self.pbytes[q]
            cap = self.pifo_cap
            while bytes_used > cap:
                pifo, node = lean_extract_max(pifo, ver)
                over = node[1]
                bytes_used -= over.length
                self.live = fat_pop(self.live, (over.rank, over.oid),
                                    None, ver, 0)[0]
                evicted.append(over.pktid)
            self.pifo[q] = pifo
            self.pbytes[q] = bytes_used
        return evicted

    def _serve(self, q, pkt, evicted, i, old_t, log):
        self.pbytes[q] -= pkt.length
        key = (pkt.rank, pkt.oid)
        self.policy.post_dequeue(pkt, pkt.rank)
        self.live, lag, rank_error = fat_pop(self.live, key, pkt.rank,
                                             self.ver, 0)
        log.append([i, 'dequeue', old_t, q, pkt.pktid, pkt.rank,
                    rank_error, lag, evicted])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- commands

    def run(self, events):
        log = []
        snaps = self.snaps
        for i, ev in enumerate(events):
            op = ev[0]
            if op == 'enqueue':
                self.cmd_enqueue(i, ev, log)
            elif op == 'dequeue':
                self.cmd_dequeue(i, ev[1], log)
            elif op == 'cancel':
                self.cmd_cancel(i, ev[1], log)
            elif op == 'inspect':
                self.cmd_inspect(i, ev[1], log)
            elif op == 'sample':
                self.cmd_sample(i, log)
            elif op == 'repartition':
                self.cmd_repartition(i, ev[1], log)
            elif op == 'weight':
                self.policy.set_weight(ev[1], ev[2])
                log.append([i, 'weight', ev[1], ev[2]])
            elif op == 'save':
                self.ver += 1
                self.policy.ver = self.ver
                snaps[ev[1]] = self.checkpoint()
                log.append([i, 'save', ev[1]])
            elif op == 'restore':
                state = snaps.get(ev[1])
                if state is not None:
                    self.restore(state)
                log.append([i, 'restore', ev[1]])
            else:
                raise ValueError('unknown command: %r' % (op,))
        return log

    def cmd_enqueue(self, i, ev, log):
        pkt = Pkt(ev[1], ev[2], ev[3], ev[4])
        pkt.oid = i
        rank = self.policy.rank_cal(pkt)
        pkt.rank = rank
        M = self.M
        R = self.R
        r = self.classify(rank)
        lb = self.l
        self.l = lb + 1
        if self.l >= self.L:
            self.l = 0
        base = lb * M * R + r
        C = self.C
        best = C[base]
        bank = 0
        for q in range(1, M):
            value = C[base + q * R]
            if value < best:
                best = value
                bank = q
        used = self.fbytes[bank]
        if used + pkt.length <= self.fifo_cap:
            self._touch_fifo(bank)
            pkt.bank = bank
            pkt.slot = len(self.fifo[bank])
            self.fifo[bank].append(pkt)
            self.fbytes[bank] = used + pkt.length
            self.fcnt[bank] += 1
            self.registry[pkt.pktid] = pkt
            self.live = fat_insert(self.live, (rank, i), pkt,
                                   self.priors.take(), self.ver)
            C[base + bank * R] += 1
            self.a += 1
            log.append([i, 'enqueue', pkt.pktid, rank, lb, r, bank, True])
            if self.a == self.period:
                self.cmd_sample(i, log)
        else:
            log.append([i, 'enqueue', pkt.pktid, rank, lb, r, bank, False])

    def cmd_dequeue(self, i, count, log):
        M = self.M
        for _ in range(count):
            old_t = self.t
            q = self.p
            nxt = q + 1
            self.p = 0 if nxt >= M else nxt
            self.t = old_t + 1
            if self.pifo[q] is not None:
                self.pifo[q], node = lean_extract_min(self.pifo[q], self.ver)
                pkt = node[1]
                self._serve(q, pkt, self._refill(q), i, old_t, log)
            else:
                evicted = self._refill(q)
                root = self.pifo[q]
                if root is not None:
                    self.pifo[q], node = lean_extract_min(root, self.ver)
                    self._serve(q, node[1], evicted, i, old_t, log)
                else:
                    log.append([i, 'dequeue', old_t, q, None, None, 0, 0,
                                evicted])

    def cmd_sample(self, i, log):
        C = self.C
        R = self.R
        M = self.M
        L = self.L
        span = M * R
        X = [0] * R
        for r in range(R):
            X[r] = sum(C[r::R])
        for l in range(L):
            low = l * span
            for r in range(R):
                column = C[low + r:low + span:R]
                smallest = min(column)
                if smallest:
                    for q in range(M):
                        C[low + q * R + r] -= smallest
        H = self.H
        for r in range(R):
            H[r] = H[r] // 2 + X[r]
        self.a = 0
        log.append([i, 'sample', X, H[:]])

    def cmd_repartition(self, i, new_borders, log):
        new_borders = [int(x) for x in new_borders]
        new_ranges = len(new_borders) - 1
        old_ranges = self.R
        total = self.L * self.M
        C = self.C
        flat = [0] * (total * new_ranges)
        for idx in range(total):
            flat[idx * new_ranges:(idx + 1) * new_ranges] = _migrate_vector(
                C[idx * old_ranges:(idx + 1) * old_ranges],
                self.borders, new_borders, new_ranges)
        self.C = flat
        self.H = _migrate_vector(self.H, self.borders, new_borders, new_ranges)
        self.borders = new_borders
        self.R = new_ranges
        log.append([i, 'repartition', new_ranges])

    def cmd_cancel(self, i, pktid, log):
        pkt = self.registry.get(pktid)
        if pkt is not None:
            key = (pkt.rank, pkt.oid)
            lag = fat_lag(self.live, key)
            if lag is not None:
                bank = pkt.bank
                if lean_find(self.pifo[bank], key) is not None:
                    stage = 'pifo'
                    self.pifo[bank] = lean_delete(self.pifo[bank], key,
                                                  self.ver)
                    self.pbytes[bank] -= pkt.length
                else:
                    stage = 'fifo'
                    self._touch_fifo(bank)
                    self.fifo[bank][pkt.slot] = None
                    self.fbytes[bank] -= pkt.length
                    self.fcnt[bank] -= 1
                self.live = fat_pop(self.live, key, None, self.ver, 0)[0]
                log.append([i, 'cancel', pktid, stage, bank, lag])
                return
        log.append([i, 'cancel', pktid, None, None, None])

    def cmd_inspect(self, i, pktid, log):
        pkt = self.registry.get(pktid)
        record = None
        if pkt is not None:
            key = (pkt.rank, pkt.oid)
            lag = fat_lag(self.live, key)
            if lag is not None:
                bank = pkt.bank
                stage = 'pifo' if lean_find(self.pifo[bank], key) is not None \
                    else 'fifo'
                record = [pkt.rank, bank, stage, pkt.length, pkt.flowid, lag]
        log.append([i, 'inspect', pktid, record])

    # ------------------------------------------------- branches and reporting

    def checkpoint(self):
        """Whole-state snapshot; O(1) for the queues, O(L*M*R) for counters."""
        return (self.t, self.p, self.l, self.a, self.R, self.borders,
                self.H[:], self.C[:], self.policy.snapshot(),
                self.pifo[:], self.fifo[:], self.fhead[:], self.fcnt[:],
                self.fbytes[:], self.pbytes[:], self.fstamp[:], self.live)

    def restore(self, state):
        (t, p, l, a, ranges, borders, history, counters, policy, pifo, fifo,
         fhead, fcnt, fbytes, pbytes, fstamp, live) = state
        self.t = t
        self.p = p
        self.l = l
        self.a = a
        self.R = ranges
        self.borders = borders
        self.H = history[:]
        self.C = counters[:]
        self.pifo = pifo[:]
        self.fifo = fifo[:]
        self.fhead = fhead[:]
        self.fcnt = fcnt[:]
        self.fbytes = fbytes[:]
        self.pbytes = pbytes[:]
        self.fstamp = fstamp[:]
        self.live = live
        self.ver += 1
        self.policy.restore(policy, self.ver)

    # ------------------------------------------------------- base class API

    def enqueue(self, pkt: Pkt) -> None:
        """Library form of an enqueue attempt; the packet carries its own id."""
        self.cmd_enqueue(pkt.oid,
                         ['enqueue', pkt.pktid, pkt.flowid, pkt.length,
                          pkt.flow_size], [])

    def dequeue(self):
        """Library form of one service opportunity; None when idle."""
        log = []
        before = len(log)
        self.cmd_dequeue(-1, 1, log)
        return None if len(log) == before else log[0]

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        if self.live is not None:
            return False
        return all(self.fcnt[q] == 0 for q in range(self.M))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ final state

    def certificate(self):
        M = self.M
        L = self.L
        R = self.R
        C = self.C
        counters = []
        for l in range(L):
            low = l * M * R
            counters.append([C[low + q * R:low + (q + 1) * R] for q in range(M)])
        queues = []
        for q in range(M):
            staged = []
            for pkt in self.fifo[q][self.fhead[q]:]:
                if pkt is not None:
                    staged.append(pkt.pktid)
            resident = []
            lean_recs(self.pifo[q], resident)
            queues.append({'fifo': staged,
                           'pifo': [pkt.pktid for pkt in resident],
                           'fifo_bytes': self.fbytes[q],
                           'pifo_bytes': self.pbytes[q]})
        pairs = []
        fat_pairs(self.live, 0, pairs)
        pairs.sort(key=lambda item: item[0].pktid)
        return {'tick': self.t,
                'load_balancer': self.l,
                'service_bank': self.p,
                'sample_progress': self.a,
                'borders': list(self.borders),
                'counters': counters,
                'history': self.H[:],
                'policy': self.policy.certificate(),
                'queues': queues,
                'lags': [[pkt.pktid, lag] for pkt, lag in pairs]}

    raise ValueError('nonfinite number')

    if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):

    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        for item in (value.values() if isinstance(value, dict) else value):
            _finite(item)


def _invalid():

def main():

            if thr is not None:

                for k in list(model):
                    if k[0] < thr: model[k] += 1
            else:
                ecnt = 0
            assert lag == elag, (step,'lag',lag,elag)
            assert cnt == ecnt, (step,'cnt',cnt,ecnt,key,sorted(model))
        # verify all lags
        pairs = []
        fat_pairs(root, 0, pairs)
        got = {p[0][1]: lag for p,lag in pairs} if False else {p.oid if False else p[1][0]: lag for p,lag in pairs}
        got = {}

        assert got == model, (step, 'pairs', got, model)
        # verify fat_lag
        for k, v in model.items():

    print('brute ok', n)

"""Staged bank scheduler (protocol 3.0).

Each physical bank owns an arrival-ordered staging FIFO and a PIFO ordered by
the immutable ``(rank, ordinal)`` of its residents.  The global live set spans
both stages of every bank and is held in one rank-ordered order-statistic tree
that also carries the live lag accounting, so priority overtakes are charged
with a single O(depth) subtree operation instead of a backlog walk.

Service opportunities are fixed and cyclic: a visit touches bank ``p`` only,
advances ``p`` and the logical tick even when nothing is served.  Historical
admission counters never decrease; sampling and repartitioning re-express them
conservatively.  Checkpoints isolate whole branches; the name registry lives
outside the saved state and never rewinds.
"""

from packet import Pkt
from algorithms import (SchedulingAlgorithm, FifoAlgorithm, SpAlgorithm,
                        pFabricAlgorithm, WFQAlgorithm, make_policy)

from treap import (Priors, lean_insert, lean_delete, lean_extract_min,
                   lean_extract_max, lean_find, lean_recs,
                   fat_insert, fat_pop, fat_charge_less, fat_lag, fat_pairs)


STAGE_CHUNK = 256


class Scheduler:
    """Baseline scheduling interface retained for library users."""

    def enqueue(self, pkt: Pkt) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")

    def dequeue(self):
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses should implement this method.")


def _migrate_vector(vector, old_borders, new_borders, new_ranges):
    """Prefix-quantized projection of one counter vector onto new ranges."""
    out = [0] * new_ranges
    ranges = len(vector)
    for j in range(ranges):
        mass = vector[j]
        if not mass:
            continue
        low = old_borders[j]
        width = old_borders[j + 1] - low
        previous = 0
        for s in range(1, new_ranges + 1):
            x = new_borders[s] - low
            if x < 0:
                x = 0
            elif x > width:
                x = width
            value = (mass * x) // width
            out[s - 1] += value - previous
            previous = value
    return out

            self.fstamp[q] = self.ver

    def _stage_append(self, q, pkt):
        """Queue a packet at the rear; returns its immutable staging slot."""
        self._touch_stage(q)
        chunks = self.fchunks[q]
        slot = self.fslot[q]

            chunks.append([self.ver, [pkt]])

                chunk = [self.ver, chunk[1][:]]
                chunks[-1] = chunk
            chunk[1].append(pkt)
        self.fslot[q] = slot + 1
        return slot

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""JSON entry point; all computation lives in the scheduling modules.

Reads one UTF-8 JSON request through EOF and writes one UTF-8 JSON response.
Invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON, duplicate keys at any depth, nonfinite values or
trailing JSON values produce exactly {"error":"invalid"} with exit zero.
"""
import gc
import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from utils import run_request


def _pairs(items):
    result = {}
    for key, value in items:
        if key in result:
            raise ValueError('duplicate key')
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _reject_constant(value):
    raise ValueError('nonfinite number')


def _finite(value):
    if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError('nonfinite number')
    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        for item in (value.values() if isinstance(value, dict) else value):
            _finite(item)


def _invalid():
    sys.stdout.write('{"error":"invalid"}\n')


def main():
    try:
        request = json.loads(sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode('utf-8'),
                             object_pairs_hook=_pairs,
                             parse_constant=_reject_constant)
        _finite(request)
        response = run_request(request)
        text = json.dumps(response, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False)
    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError,
            UnicodeError, RecursionError, OverflowError):
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr)
        _invalid()
        return
    sys.stdout.write(text)
    sys.stdout.write('\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    gc.disable()
    main()

"""Ordered-storage module: versioned copy-on-write treaps (protocol 3.0).

Two node layouts are used, both plain lists so that copying a node is a single
slice and an isolated checkpoint of a whole structure is one root reference:

  lean  [key, rec, prio, left, right, stamp]                   bank PIFOs
  fat   [key, rec, prio, left, right, size, val, lazy, stamp]  global live set

``key``   ordering key; ``(rank, ordinal)`` tuples for both layouts.
``rec``   the packet record that occupies the node.
``prio``  treap priority (deterministic, structural only).
``size``  subtree population (fat layout), used for rank-order statistics.
``val``   the node's own accumulated lag (fat layout).
``lazy``  a pending lag addition for every node of the subtree (fat layout).
``stamp`` version the node was produced in.  A node is copied before its first
          mutation in a later version, so saved checkpoints stay immutable while
          taking or reloading a checkpoint costs O(1).

Lag is stored as ``val + lazy`` per node, therefore "every remaining strictly
lower-rank resident gains one lag" is a single O(depth) subtree operation and
never walks the backlog.
"""

M64 = (1 << 64) - 1


class Priors:
    """Deterministic treap priority source; structure only, never observable."""

    __slots__ = ('state',)

        z = s ^ (s >> 30)
        z = (z * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & M64
        z ^= z >> 27
